subject: Demo recap + proposed validation roadmap — Sunward Energy
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@sunwardenergy.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + proposed validation roadmap — Sunward Energy

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for your time on today’s demo. Appreciate the candid feedback and the clear priorities you called out (low-latency inference for internal ops, predictable per-query cost, and stronger controls around data residency). Attached is a short validation roadmap and the sample data schema we discussed. High level proposal: a focused 3-week validation to prove performance and fit before a wider pilot.

Quick recap of what we showed and why it maps to your goals:
- Low-latency path: our Dedicated runtime with latency-first routing and KV prefix caching to keep p95 down for short queries.
- Cost controls: batching policy + per-route token caps and our Optimize suggestions for quantization that keep unit cost predictable.
- Security: private deployment options and audit logs; we can scope a VPC/managed KMS setup for the pilot.

Proposed 3-week validation (high level) — please review and flag changes:
Week 0 (prep, 3–5 days): dataset ingestion (sample subset), access provisioning, baseline metric capture.
Week 1 (benchmarks, 5 working days): throughput/latency runs at expected concurrency (p50/p95/p99), failure-mode simulation, and cost projection.
Week 2 (quality & ops, 5 working days): accuracy/regression checks vs your current model outputs using curated prompts, monitoring runbooks, and rollback policy validation.

Success criteria (pass/fail for go/no-go):
- Accuracy: model outputs must be within 5% of your current label-based baseline on core prompts (precision/recall where applicable).
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for single-turn queries at target concurrency, 99th < 350ms.
- Cost: estimated steady-state unit cost <= $0.0025/token for your expected mix (we'll refine with real telemetry).
- Ops: ability to run a trace and get token-level cost + latency breakdowns from Console within 10 minutes of an incident.

Ownership & next steps:
- Sunward: provide sample dataset (CSV export) and a short list of 15 representative prompts/questions — target by Mon 6/15.
- Redwood: share POC environment credentials, ingest script, and a benchmark runbook by Tue 6/16.
- Schedule: propose kickoff sync Tues 6/16 10:00am PT (30m).

Attachments: Sunward-POC-outline.xlsx, sample-data-schema.csv

If this looks reasonable I’ll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and loop in our security lead for a short call on data handling.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear outline. This looks like the kind of tight validation we need. A couple quick questions before we lock in kickoff:
1) Data & retention: we need to confirm retention is configurable and logs can be excluded from S3 exports. Can you share a short dataflow note and any controls around retention windows?
2) SOC2: our security team asked for a recent SOC2 snapshot and the names of any subprocessors you use.
3) Cost estimate: the $0.0025/token is helpful — can you provide a worked example for ~10M tokens/month to show the expected monthly spend ranges?

We’ll aim to get the sample dataset and 15 prompts to you by EOD Mon (Priya will coordinate). Kickoff on Tue 6/16 10:00am PT works for us.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Data Products | Sunward Energy

Dylan / Ben —

For Alex's questions, quick notes we can share on kickoff:
- Retention: POC environments default to 30-day KV cache retention but we can set to customer-defined windows or disable retention entirely. Audit logs are stored for X days by default but we support export and retention policies per-customer (we'll provide the policy doc).
- SOC2 & subprocessors: attaching a SOC2-snapshot.pdf we can share now. Subprocessors include our cloud infra partner (CNP Cloud Services) and analytics partner (Streamlook). We'll confirm the subprocessors list in the security call.
- Cost worked example: for 10M tokens/month we can generate a 3-tier cost projection (baseline, optimized batching, caching benefits). I’ll prepare a short spreadsheet snippet for the kickoff.

I recommend we add our security engineering lead (Ben) to the 20m slot right after kickoff to answer the SOC2/retention questions so Alex and Priya have direct contact. Ben — can you join Tue 6/16 10:30am PT?

-Lauren
